children: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Tuesday said India aims to achieve defence production worth Rs 3 lakh crore and defence exports of Rs 50,000 crore by 2029, while stressing the need to accelerate military modernisation and strengthen indigenous defence capabilities.

Chairing a meeting of the Ministry of Defence's Consultative Committee on ‘Modernisation of Indian Defence Forces’ in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan, Singh said the government was committed to building a technologically empowered military capable of addressing present-day and emerging security challenges.
The meeting, held on Tuesday, discussed changing warfare patterns, technological advancements and the need to improve the operational preparedness of the Army, Navy and Air Force.

According to the Defence Ministry, the discussions focused on six broad areas: capability development and force modernisation, jointness among the three services, indigenous defence manufacturing, emerging technologies, defence research and innovation, and resource optimisation.
Singh highlighted the government's focus on budgetary support, capital acquisition, technology development and human resources to prepare the armed forces for technology-driven warfare.
The Defence Minister said the defence budget for 2026-27 had been increased to a record Rs 7.85 lakh crore, including a capital outlay of Rs 2.19 lakh crore for modernisation and capital procurement.

He said defence production had increased from Rs 46,429 crore in 2014-15 to a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore in 2025-26. Defence exports, which were below Rs 2,000 crore in 2014, had grown to approximately Rs 40,000 crore, according to the ministry.
“We aim to achieve defence production worth Rs 3 lakh crore and defence exports worth Rs 50,000 crore by 2029,” Singh said.

He also underlined the importance of reducing India's strategic dependence on foreign sources through domestic research, design, development and manufacturing. The government is encouraging greater participation from private companies, start-ups, micro, small and medium enterprises and academic institutions in the defence ecosystem.
AI, Autonomous Systems And Military Preparedness

The meeting also discussed the growing role of artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, unmanned platforms, cyber and space capabilities, electronic warfare and advanced communications in future conflicts.

Singh highlighted the contribution of the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) in developing advanced weapons, missiles and military systems. He called for stronger collaboration between the armed forces, DRDO, defence public sector undertakings, private industry and academic institutions to translate research into operational capabilities.

On human resources and military preparedness, the Defence Minister said modernisation should not be limited to acquiring new weapons and equipment but must also improve the capabilities and readiness of military personnel.
He referred to new formations introduced by the Indian Army, including the Asani, Bhairav and Shaktiban platoons, saying they were proving effective in meeting contemporary operational requirements.
The meeting also emphasised stronger coordination among the three services, joint operational planning and the integrated use of capabilities across multiple domains.

Members of Parliament from both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha offered suggestions during the deliberations. The ministry said the discussions resulted in a roadmap focused on prioritising critical military capabilities, improving coordination among stakeholders, streamlining acquisition and development processes, and periodically reviewing progress.
